Resilient Nowcasting

Predicting Spatio-Temporal Dynamics from Incomplete Urban Sensor Data

Carrow Morris-Wiltshire

Supervisors: Prof. Phil James, Dr Sheen Cabaneros & Keith Hermiston (DSTL)
EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Geospatial Systems • Newcastle University

1

The Challenge

Municipal IoT sensor networks — critical for urban intelligence — suffer from three pervasive operational challenges that undermine conventional forecasting models:

⚡
Null-Zero Conflation: Raw sensor telemetry records genuine zero activity and sensor transmission failures identically as null values, creating a fundamentally ambiguous training signal.
🌐
Non-Euclidean Spatial Dependencies: Sensor interactions are governed by road topologies and urban land-use morphology, not simple Euclidean proximity.
📡
Dynamic Network Topology: Sensors are frequently decommissioned or temporarily offline, requiring inductive spatial inference without retraining.
2

Research Aim & Approach

To develop a resilient spatio-temporal nowcasting model that accurately predicts urban pedestrian flow, even with incomplete or missing sensor data.

Progressive Experimental Structure

1
Temporal Forecasting & Missingness: Single-sensor baselines (ARIMA, LSTM, GRU) characterising how missing data regimes affect predictive fidelity.
2
Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention: Introduces GATv2 graph neural networks to quantify the gain from incorporating inter-sensor spatial relationships.
3
Resilient End-to-End Pipeline (RIOT): Full integration: dynamic graph learning, masked auto-encoding, multi-task decoders (imputation + forecasting + zero-shot spatial kriging), and probabilistic ZINB loss.
3

Data & Sensor Network

Pedestrian counts from the Newcastle Urban Observatory — 48 sensors across the city at 15-minute resolution.

15-Dimensional Static Feature Vector

Each sensor node is characterised by urban morphology features used for dynamic topology inference:

Transit Count Retail Count Food & Drink Nightlife Education Recreation Total POI
Land-use Entropy School Zone Dist. to Centre
Betweenness Closeness Degree Bus Stops Parking

Structural MNAR Masks

The model receives two explicit binary missingness channels as first-class input features — a total MNAR mask (any null) and a night MNAR mask (null ∩ 00:00–05:00) — enabling the model to distinguish sensor failure from genuine inactivity.

4

RIOT Pipeline Architecture

The four-component architecture decouples spatial topology learning, spatial message passing, temporal sequence processing, and task-specific decoding:

Figure 1 — Complete RIOT pipeline: Dynamic Graph Learner infers topology from static urban features → GATv2 Spatial Encoder with edge-conditioned attention → Transformer Temporal Encoder → Three decoupled decoder heads (imputation, forecasting, kriging) with joint loss optimisation.

5

ZINB Loss & Uncertainty Quantification

The forecasting head optimises a Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial likelihood, explicitly modelling the bimodal missingness of urban count data:

P(yi | μi, θi, πi) = πi + (1 − πi) · NB(0 | μi, θi)   if yi = 0
(1 − πi) · NB(yi | μi, θi)   if yi > 0
μ Mean Count Expected pedestrian flow
θ Dispersion Variance / uncertainty
π Zero Probability Dropout vs. empty

Decoupled Normalisation: Encoder inputs are z-scored for gradient stability. Forecast targets remain as raw integer counts — preserving the discrete domain required by the NB likelihood. Traffic and weather use separate scalers to prevent cross-domain contamination.

Operational Reliability Framework

GREEN Direct Observation Sensor active, high data coverage. Model acts as denoiser.
AMBER High-Confidence Inference Sensor failed, but strong spatial connections to reliable neighbours.
RED Low-Confidence Isolated node — high uncertainty. Require eyes-on verification.
7

Future Directions

🌍
Transfer Learning: Pre-train on data-rich environments (Newcastle Urban Observatory) to learn universal physics of urban movement, then fine-tune on sparse, ad-hoc networks for rapid deployment.
⚙️
Linear Attention Scalability: Replace O(N²) graph attention with linear approximations (e.g. Performer) to scale to city-wide networks with 1000+ sensors.
📱
Edge Deployment: Optimise models for distributed inference directly on sensor hardware, reducing bandwidth dependency and enabling real-time local decision-making.
🏙️
Graph-Size Agnostic Architectures: Explore hierarchical pooling and meta-learning strategies for cross-city generalisation without per-graph retraining.

Probabilistic Nowcasts Under Real Outages

Figure 2 — Two days of 15-minute pedestrian counts: ZINB mean μ (orange line) with θ-driven 95% dispersion band and π dropout probability (purple). During the shaded outage window the model widens uncertainty and raises π instead of collapsing to zero — missingness is forecast, not conflated with absence.

Calibration: Before → After

Figure 3 — Probability Integral Transform histograms. Early runs were underdispersed (left); the final model’s near-uniform PIT (right, run radiant-dawn-8) confirms its predictive distributions are well calibrated.
